_comment: Why a generator that was going to be benchmarked is not in the benchmark.
PySynthea (tietai-synthea) was the obvious third generator: pip-installable, no JVM,
231 disease modules, FHIR R4 export. This repository's own README concedes that it
removes the 'no Java' differentiator. It cannot be scored, and the reason is recorded
here rather than left as an unexplained absence from the results table.
Its FHIR export emits Observations without values. A systolic blood pressure comes out
with status 'final', no value[x] and no dataAbsentReason, which is not a measurement.
Every analyte the fidelity benchmarks read is in this state.
python3.12 -m venv env && env/bin/pip install tietai-synthea

_note: Systolic, diastolic, height and weight are all present and all valueless.
Glucose, HDL, triglycerides, HbA1c, ALT and AST likewise.
The 60 valued observations are pain scores, temperatures, DXA T-scores, FEV1/FVC,
PSA, NT-proBNP and magnesium — none of which any fidelity benchmark here reads.
No configuration option governs this; FHIR export is on by default and was used.

hl7_validator._comment: org.hl7.fhir.core validator_cli, FHIR R4 4.0.1, one bundle.

top_errors.issue: If a date has a time, it must have a timezone
Unknown code 'AMBULATORY' in v3-ActCode (the code is 'AMB')
Wrong display name 'Vital-Signs' for the observation-category code
Array cannot be empty - the property should not be present
Coding.system must be an absolute reference — it emits 'LOINC', not http://loinc.org

conclusion: Not scored, because there is nothing to score. This is reported as a measurement
with its reproduction rather than as a criticism: the finding is that the FHIR
export is not yet analysable, not that the project is without merit. Its module
coverage and JVM-free install are real.
It does mean this repository's README was too generous. 'No Java is no longer a
reason to pick this project' assumed the alternative produced usable output.
